uncertainty.basis: 95 % half-width of each sample SD from 4000 trials; the 99.9 % chi-square intervals contain the prediction for 6/6 pairs

basis.notes: No images were acquired; real noise is signal dependent, spatially correlated and marker detectors interpolate below one pixel.

findings.claim: Real image noise is Gaussian with sigma = 0.25 px and marker localization rounds to whole pixels

hypothesis: Rounding to integer pixels after Gaussian noise gives error variance sigma^2 + 1/12 when the true coordinate is uniformly placed on the pixel grid, and chord standard deviations follow linear propagation through the triangulation Jacobian.
input_data: Markers at s = [0.0, 0.015, 0.03, 0.045, 0.06, 0.075, 0.09, 0.105, 0.12] m along helices alpha = [0.0, 45.0, 90.0] deg (27/27 visible in both images)
mathematical_model: e = round(x + n) - x = n + q; with frac(x) ~ U(0,1) independent of n, q ~ U(-1/2, 1/2) is independent of n, so Var e = sigma^2 + 1/12. sigma_c^2 = (sigma^2 + 1/12) sum_j J_j^2 (8 pixel coordinates per pair).
numerical_result: additivity max |z| = 1.37; aligned variance 0.00e+00 vs 0.0933; chord propagation max |z| = 1.81, predicted SD inside the 99.9 % interval for 6/6 pairs.
observation_model: Synthetic pixels with a uniform grid phase drawn independently per marker, camera and axis, Gaussian noise and integer rounding.
